claude.sample_unit: referral records (Chilean Waiting List Corpus); count not reported

links.outcome: Performance drop after label-set/task-definition shift, with and without retraining on new-period data
links.effect: Supervised models dropped up to 82% F1 in LSI and 43% in TDE; continual retraining gradually restored performance and surpassed ICL/hybrid after at least 30% of new data.
links.quote: Continual adaptation with incremental retraining gradually restored performance, but only surpassed in-context and hybrid approaches after incorporating at least 30% of data from the second period.

links.outcome: Performance degradation of static clinical NLP models under distributional and task-definition drift
links.effect: Conventional supervised models showed severe degradation, up to 82% F1 drop in LSI and 43% in TDE.
links.quote: Conventional supervised models showed severe degradation under these shifts (up to a drop of 82% F1 in LSI and 43% in TDE).

links.outcome: Recovery of performance and error rates after retraining on new-period data
links.effect: After retraining on period B, FNR and FPR decreased markedly toward baseline; the confusion-matrix diagonal was largely restored in LSI.
links.quote: After retraining on period B data, both FNR and FPR decreased markedly, approaching baseline levels.

links.outcome: Model performance when applied to a new label set or task definition (new context)
links.effect: Legacy models trained on period A had severe F1 drops on period B; both FNR and FPR increased substantially in TDE.
links.quote: When the model trained on period A was directly evaluated on period B without retraining, both error rates increased substantially relative to the baseline evaluation on period A.

unlisted_practices: Hybrid approach pairing legacy discriminative model with LLM agent that overrides outdated predictions after task definition change
Prompt-based in-context adaptation (optimized instructions) to new label sets/task definitions without retraining
Simulation framework parameterizing label-set and task-definition shift severity for benchmarking model robustness

links.outcome: F1 drop on shifted period B data
links.effect: Conventional supervised models dropped up to 82% F1 in LSI and 43% in TDE.
links.quote: Conventional supervised models showed severe degradation under these shifts (up to a drop of 82% F1 in LSI and 43% in TDE).

links.effect: In-context learning drops were 35% LSI and 10% TDE; hybrid limited drops to approximately 8%.
links.quote: In contrast, in-context learning reduced the drop to 35% in LSI and 10% in TDE, while a hybrid method further improved robustness, limiting the drop to approximately 8% in both settings.

links.effect: Severe performance drops occurred: up to 82% in F1 for LSI and 43% for TDE.
links.quote: In line with previous evidence from conventional machine learning studies on data set shift and temporal drift [ 4 , 11 , 14 ], we also observe severe performance drops, up to 82% in F1 for LSI and 43% for TDE, which underscores the risks of deploying fixed models in evolving clinical environments.

links.effect: Retraining with as little as 20% of period B data reduced TDE drops to minimal levels.
links.quote: In the TDE scenario (Fig. 3 b), a similar trend was observed: all simulation strengths began with high performance drop, but retraining with as little as 20% of period B data reduced the drop to minimal levels.

unlisted_practices: Use in-context learning prompts with current label space or task definitions to adapt clinical NLP models without new labeled data.
Use a hybrid LLM agent that considers a legacy model suggestion and overrides it when inconsistent with updated rules.
Parameterized simulation of label-set incompatibility and task definition evolution for clinical NLP robustness benchmarking.
